Residual: unrecognized systematic effect or measurement model.

Differential environmental coupling by location: lab instruments mechanically coupled to each other (creating decorrelation via phase inversion), observatory instruments isolated from lab but responding to separate environmental driver (e.g., diurnal thermal cycle) with 3-day phase lag relative to lab; pendulum_lab–resonator_obs correlation reflects cross-location thermal or acoustic diffusion.

Baseline period (days 1–10) was too short; instruments still in non-stationary thermal settling with instrument-type-specific time constants, creating spurious correlations and decorrelations by coincidence rather than true coupling.

Unrecognized systematic error in correlation computation or lag-search algorithm, specifically biasing the pendulum_lab–resonator_obs pair positive or inflating its correlation estimate through multiple-comparison bias, indexing error, unequal normalization, or hidden data transformation.

Unmeasured multi-component environmental confounder (temperature, humidity, pressure, acoustic vibration, electromagnetic noise) with differential coupling across instrument types and locations, creating the observed partition between lab and observatory without requiring mechanical coupling within the lab.

Procedural or operator error (inconsistent release, grip, timing, data entry) that introduces correlated noise differing by instrument type or location, specifically decorrelating instruments recorded under different conditions (e.g., morning lab sessions vs. afternoon observatory sessions).

Hardware malfunction (creep, saturation, misalignment, drift, damping change) in one or more instruments, producing spurious decorrelation or anomalous correlation via low variance, fixed repetitions, or nonlinear response.

Residual: unrecognized systematic effect or measurement model not yet articulated—including nonlinear coupling through building infrastructure, procedurally-mediated environmental effects (heat from body during sessions affecting distant instrument via thermal diffusion), data-entry errors in one stream, or misinterpretation of a particular trial sequence.
